goals.0: Asking the price: Wie viel kostet das?
goals.1: Saying prices in euros and cents (2,50 €)
goals.2: Paying the bill at the counter or by card
dialog.0.de.2.n: kostet for one thing, kosten for several
dialog.1.de.4.n: Euro stays the same in the plural: zwei Euro
dialog.2.de.4.n: ich nehme — nehmen is irregular: du nimmst
dialog.3.de.1.n: „Das macht …“ = That comes to … in total
dialog.5.de.0.n: Said when handing something to someone
grammar.0.title: Saying prices
grammar.0.intro: The number before the comma is Euro, the number after it is Cent. „Euro“ and „Cent“ stay the same in the plural.
grammar.0.note: The decimal sign is a comma (,): 2,50 — German uses a comma where English uses a point.
grammar.1.intro: nehmen is irregular: with du and er, e → i and the h is dropped.
grammar.1.note: Just like essen: ich esse — du isst; ich nehme — du nimmst.
grammar.2.title: kostet or kosten?
grammar.2.text: For one item: „Das kostet …“. For several: „Die Äpfel kosten …“. In questions: „Wie viel kostet das?“ / „Wie viel kosten die Äpfel?“ — the verb agrees with the number of things being bought.
quiz.7.prompt: Put the words in order to make the question: “How much does this cost?”
